articles.author: The Thorn - NYC DSA Electoral Working Group
articles.content_excerpt: Local News In a video collaboration with New York City Councilmember Chi Osse (Council District 36, Bedford–Stuyvesant), Mayor Zohran Mamdani announced the official disbandment of the NYPD’s Strategic Response Group (SRG), addressing a campaign promise to separate protest response from counterterrorism functions. articles.content_excerpt: Caregivers looking after children of any age, but especially young ones, must offer proper nourishment and hydration, mental clarity, flexibility, a sense of joy, a sense of safety, and the ability to communicate clearly. articles.title: Stella Lefty: Data Center Music
articles.author: Nikil Soto
articles.content_excerpt: When Stella Lefty wrote the chorus to “Boston,” she was waiting in Nashville for a boy from outside Atlanta. Why Boston? She had a gig coming up there, she told Taste of Country . A month later she noticed it was also the name on the piano. Lefty posted the chorus on TikTok before there were verses to go with it. “Boston,” the breakout single from her debut album, Long Way Home , reached number two on the Billboard Hot 100 and number one on country radio. Try saying “I like it when you’re nice to me” aloud. Now hear how her bright, raspy voice tumbles into it over the acoustic guitar , pleased and a little embarrassed at what she’s admitted. articles.title: Effective Altruism Is Increasingly Just Funding Itself
articles.author: Jacob Davis
articles.content_excerpt: The basic pitch for effective altruism (EA) is simple: charitable giving is an investment, whose return is in others’ well-being rather than your financial betterment. Given that it’s an investment, it makes sense to look for a strong, measurable return from wherever you choose to donate. After all, if you really care about others being well-off, you should be at least as conscientious about these investments as you are about your retirement savings. This is, to say the least, a controversial approach to charity. It has many detractors: those who argue that the approach flattens value to numbers in a spreadsheet, or that it ignores the place of solidarity and political organizing. articles.title: New Deal Majority
articles.author: John Peeler
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. Since the Civil War, scholars have found a persistent pattern in party competition in this country. One party tends to win the majority of votes nationally for several consecutive elections. Then some critical event such as a depression leads a critical mass of voters to switch loyalties. The former minority party becomes the normal majority. After the Civil War, the Republicans were the normal majority, narrowly until 1896, then overwhelmingly until the Great Depression. The shock of the Depression and the vigor of the New Deal response then established the Democrats as the normal majority until the late 1960s. articles.content_excerpt: By Nikos Mottas November 11, 2026 In Defense of Communism Seventy years after the counterrevolutionary events of 1956, Hungary remains a powerful reminder that the struggle between socialism and capitalism does not end with the overthrow of bourgeois power. articles.title: The Limits of Going it Alone: Lessons from Dan Osborn’s Defeat in Nebraska
articles.author: MLToday
articles.content_excerpt: By Les Leopold November 4, 2026 lesleopold.substack.com Dan Osborn, the independent candidate and former local union president, once again came within a few percentage points of winning the Nebraska U.S. Senate seat. (He lost by 6.7% in 2024 and the same again this year.) He mounted an impressive challenge, but he couldn’t close the gap. Why? And what does his defeat tell us about the future of independent working-class politics? Wouldn’t Osborn have done much better if he ran as a Democrat? The anti-Trump Blue Wave created key red state Senate Democratic victories as it tore through Texas, Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, South Carolina, and maybe even Mississippi. But, it hit the shoals in North Dakota where the Democrat lost by 20.7 percent, by 18 percent in Oklahoma, and by 30.4 percent in Wyoming.
